name: Sulfasalazine
route_note: Oral tablets or enteric-coated tablets in divided doses; suppositories or enemas in some countries

discovery.by: Nanna Svartz, Karolinska Institute, with Pharmacia
discovery.note: Designed by linking a sulfonamide antibacterial to an anti-inflammatory salicylate, on the theory that rheumatoid arthritis had an infectious cause.

tagline: Sulfonamide–salicylate prodrug for ulcerative colitis and rheumatoid arthritis
summary: Sulfasalazine is an azo-linked combination of sulfapyridine and 5-aminosalicylic acid, split by colonic bacteria. Designed in Sweden for rheumatoid arthritis, it became a long-standing treatment for ulcerative colitis and remains a conventional DMARD for inflammatory arthritis.
mechanism: Little sulfasalazine is absorbed intact. Colonic bacterial azoreductases cleave it into 5-ASA, which acts locally on the colonic mucosa, and sulfapyridine, which is absorbed.

In arthritis, benefit is attributed to sulfasalazine itself and sulfapyridine, which inhibit NF-κB activation, cytokine production and lymphocyte and neutrophil function, and increase adenosine release.
uses: Psoriatic arthritis and axial spondyloarthritis (off-label in some regions)

history.title: Development
history.detail: Nanna Svartz develops salicylazosulfapyridine with Pharmacia.

history.title: Introduced
history.detail: Salazopyrin is introduced in Sweden for rheumatoid arthritis and ulcerative colitis.

history.title: US approval
history.detail: Sulfasalazine (Azulfidine) is approved in the US.

history.title: 5-ASA identified
history.detail: Oxford researchers show that 5-ASA is its active moiety in colitis, leading to mesalazine products.

history.title: Rheumatoid arthritis in the US
history.detail: Azulfidine EN-tabs gain US approval for rheumatoid arthritis.

pk.half_life: ~7.6 h (parent); sulfapyridine 6–14 h depending on acetylator status
pk.metabolism: Colonic azoreduction; sulfapyridine acetylated by NAT2 and hydroxylated

common: Orange-yellow discolouration of urine and skin

facts: Sulfasalazine was one of the first drugs deliberately designed for rheumatoid arthritis.
Slow acetylators have higher sulfapyridine levels and more adverse effects.
